title: Higher-Round Multiple-Tweak Differential Bias in SCARF
summary: The source provides smaller-round bias formulas, but the higher-round interaction of the two functions and its effect on differential bias remains unresolved.

formal_statement.body: For higher-round multiple-tweak differential analysis of SCARF, characterize how the differential properties of the S-box $S$ interact with those of $S^{-1}(S(\cdot \oplus k))$, where $k$ is the tweak parameter, and determine how this interaction affects the estimation of differential bias. The available formulas multiply probabilities of differential transitions through $S$ by the EDP for a transition over a smaller number of rounds in which $S^{-1}\circ S(\cdot \oplus k)$ plays a role, but the interaction between these two functions and its influence on the bias remain unresolved. The characterization should apply to the difference values used in the bias computation.

scope.domain: Symmetric cryptanalysis, specifically higher-round multiple-tweak differential analysis of SCARF.
parameters: S, the S-box whose differential properties are considered
Difference values used in the bias computation
scope.unresolved_remainder: Characterize the interaction between the differential properties of the S-box and the function S^{-1}(S(· ⊕ k)) in higher-round multiple-tweak analysis, and determine its effect on estimating differential bias for the difference values used in the computation.

progress.summary: The source explicitly presents the interaction of the two functions and its influence on bias as an open question after describing formulas that combine differential-transition probabilities through the S-box with an EDP for a smaller-round transition involving the shifted inverse composition.
citation_labels: Christina Boura et al., Multiple-Tweak Differential Attack Against SCARF
